chapter.title: Chapter Six: The Function
chapter.subtitle: The room is bigger than the rivalry.
chapter.description: Keep the fundraiser open while the brothers agree to fair entry.

tips: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Welcome to the fundraiser. Food money keeps these events running. Three-table qualifier tonight gets you to the championship round. I'm Bottle Girl, I'm covering bar, and you're my first table.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Straightening up.)* Bet. *(Beat.)* We doing the qualifier or we doing the tasting?

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: We're doing the—

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Because Terrence's open, and I want it noted it's *open*, and I want it noted *before* you start, so nobody can say afterward that nobody was told.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: I don't know what Terrence's is.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Genuine pain.)* It's the *rebrand*, ma'am.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, not even trying to be subtle.)* He renamed it.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I *strategically* repositioned it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He renamed it Terrence's.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, urgently, like you're his only lawyer.)*I got rid of the *Liquid Gold*. I got rid of *my* name on it. That's not a rebrand, that's a *humble*. A man can only build a ceiling if he

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: steps back from the *name*, and I stepped back from the name. *(Beat.)*It's Terrence's. It's *his*. It was *always* his, that's the whole premise, I been saying that since March.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Since March?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Since March.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's September.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I've been *saying* it since March. That's called *consistency*, ma'am, that's a whole thing people look for.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: *(Pointing.)* Is that the same cooler.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's a cooler.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: It's a cooler with a *hinge problem*. I've seen that cooler. That cooler made a *noise*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Long beat.)* ...That's Terrence's cooler.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: That is the *same* cooler.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's a cooler *in the Terrence family*. *(Beat.)* What, you want me to put my name on the *equipment* too? Where does it end? Where does it *end*? At what point do I own a *spoon*?

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: *(Opening the cooler.)* Is — *(Beat.)* Is that cheese under a *lid*?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's a *feature*.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: It's a *plate*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's a *nine-dollar lid*, and I will die on this.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Instantly, and she's been waiting six weeks for this.)*Church Auntie told me. In September. She said she went in there to bless the food and there was a *situation*, and she said, and I am

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: quoting, "I don't need a cheese incident before I bless this food," and then she pulled the plug on it.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: She unplugged it?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: She unplugged it like a woman ending a *situation*.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: *(Looking in the cooler.)* Does it keep moving?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Quietly.)* ...Don't answer that.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Why not?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* 'Cause if it moves, it's a *second* lid, and I got a *brand*.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, because she's the boss and she's efficient.)* You're the one with the entry sheet. So — how many did you buy?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's a *new* thing. It's new. It's *pre-launch*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It launched. In chapter two. At this tournament.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It launched *soft*.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: How many.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: ...I got a *loyalty* thing. It's coming.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Cornball.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *One.* *(Beat.)*And the one is standing right there, and I'd like to *thank* them for their early support, and I'd like to ask them — in front of *witnesses* — whether they'd like to sample the

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: new configuration.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: First win. *(She's already moving.)*Entry sheet's to the bar. I'm covering the second table too, because the other guy double-booked *himself*, and I'll be honest with you, I don't think that was

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: an accident.

postDialogue.speaker: Live Streamer
postDialogue.text: Both brothers won their openers. *(Consulting a phone.)* Blue asked if we could put his result in a larger font.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: Same size for everybody.

postDialogue.speaker: Live Streamer
postDialogue.text: He said — and I'm quoting — "It's not about size, it's about *presence*."

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: It's about *font*. He can be as present as he likes, he's got the same font as everybody. *(Beat.)* Somebody tell him that includes his name tag.

postDialogue.speaker: Live Streamer
postDialogue.text: He asked about the name tag *specifically*.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: He's not getting a *bigger name tag*, Reginald.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: This thing staying here or going home with you?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It's got my sign on it.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: That's a *piece of laminate*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It's got a *brand* on it, ma'am.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: *(Already lifting it.)* And what's *in* it?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: I got one more *configuration* in here. *(Beat.)* And I can't say what it is 'cause if I say it out loud, then it's out loud, and I got a *process* now.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: *(Carrying it off.)* Aisle two. By the tent. Don't touch anybody's tent.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Yes ma'am. *(Beat, to the player, automatic.)* Nine dollars. It's always nine dollars.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Welcome to my second job. Please don't put your deck on the wet part of the bar.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Where's the dry part.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: There *isn't* one. That's the *joke*. Everybody asks me that and then acts surprised for about ninety seconds.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I put it on the napkin.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Thank you. Somebody tell the *next* person that, I have been saying it for *four hours*.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: I brought the contender sheets. And before anybody says anything, Blue *asked* me to bring them.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Loud, immediately.)* He *asked.*

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: He asked! With *words*! I want that in a *record*, Cornball, because in *six years* of doing this for free, that has happened *twice*, and one of the times was *yesterday*, and the other time is

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *right now*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(From across the bar, not turning.)* It was a *sentence*, Alley. It's not a *thing*.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: It's a *thing* to *me*, Blue, and I'll take the *thing*.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Quietly, to the player, holding the sheets.)* He signed both of them *together*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's a good thing.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. *(Beat.)* It is.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Family counseling by office supply. *(Beat.)* That's a *good* bit. That's a *great* bit. Don't anybody *use* that.

preDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
preDialogue.text: Win this and Promoter's your last qualifier, and then you can finally eat something.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: The rules for the championship round — is that still one list?

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: *(From the door.)*It's one list, it's always one list, and nobody moves anybody's name, and I'll say it every night for a week. *(Beat.)*The moment a *hand* comes off that bar, everybody on the

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: sheet is out, including whoever the hand belonged to. That's not a *rule I invented*. That's the *first* rule. It's the only one I've got.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Not turning around.)* Noted.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: You heard me? Both of you?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I heard it.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Good. *(Beat.)* Somebody write it down.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Already writing.)* I'm on it.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: Two. Promoter's waiting by the next table. *(Beat.)* And take a plate.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I'm fine.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: It's not *for* you, it's for the *next* one, because a man who plays hungry plays *stupid*, and if he plays stupid out there, that's my *table* that people remember and I don't like it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Taking it.)* That's the first thing anybody's given me tonight for no reason.

postDialogue.speaker: Bottle Girl
postDialogue.text: *(Beat — and she's not warm, she's just accurate.)* That's because you *took* it without doing a bit, and on a night like this that's a *rarity*. *(Beat.)* Sit. Eat. Promoter's got nine minutes.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(To the room, generally.)* Quick question and it's not for anybody in particular. Who *wrote* the flyer?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Red writes the flyer.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I write the *copy*. Snitch does the *poster*.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I do the poster *and* I get paid for it, and nobody's ever *noticed* that, and it's been *six years*.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: Whoever wrote it, it said everybody plays.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: It said anybody can play.

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: It says everybody. *(Beat.)*That's a different sentence and it's been wrong for about eleven years and nobody's *fixed* it, because fixing it means somebody has to *admit* it was wrong, and around

postDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
postDialogue.text: here that's a whole *evening*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Fix it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Champion. That is the *most* dangerous sentence anybody's said on this block in *four years*, and you have said it *loudly*, at a *bar*, and about *paperwork*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Writing.)**(Beat.)*Okay. *(Beat.)*I'm writing it down, and I'm writing the *date*, and I am going to be *extremely annoying* about it every single week until it's *fixed*, and that's my *whole

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: personality* now, so you've *done* that.

phases.description: At round 4, the opponent gains 1 Motion once.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Last qualifier. Beat me and you're in. Blue and Cracked Head already cleared their side.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Both of us. Like I said we would.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Then stop asking which time slot they put me in.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Nobody moves anyone's entry. I've told both of you: tamper with the list and you're out of the title race.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: They heard you. I made copies.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: Good. Champ, ready? I'd like to do the part of my job that involves cards.

postDialogue.speaker: Promoter
postDialogue.text: Qualified. All three of you have a place for the championship round. We'll post the final order tomorrow and nobody's changing it after that, that's not how I do business.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: So will I.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I'll be there.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Excellent. Now be here for cleanup. Those chairs have been waiting patiently to be related to you.

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: *(Off, in the doorway, holding two plates and looking for a table.)* — told you the car would make it. I've been here since the second match. I got turned around at the bar twice.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(First, reflexively, and it's the wrong reflex and he knows it.)* You have a crew?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I have a cousin.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: One cousin.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: One cousin.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Champ. That one came in at the second match. Sat by the door, didn't drink, didn't talk to anybody, watched you lose to a guy called Promoter, and then went back outside. *Beat.* They've been

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: doing that all night. Every round, the door, then outside.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: You *know*?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: They drove six hours. I wasn't going to ask them to sit through the part where I'm bad at this.

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: Six hours is nothing. Six hours is a Saturday.

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: I've been sitting outside since the second match. You lost to the promoter. You lost to the guy with the cut on his hand. Blue's boy came in here and he didn't look at me once, and neither did

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: Red's, and I sat out there and I thought, okay, that's the door working, that's the thing you told me about, that's why you came.

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: And then about an hour ago a woman brought me a plate. *Beat.* Nobody asked her to. She looked at the sticker on my chest like she was reading a form, and then she brought me a plate anyway, and

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: sat with me for about ten minutes and didn't say one word about the tournament.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: It's a function. We feed people. It isn't a thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: Ma'am, I'm not complaining about the food. *(Beat.)* I'm asking why the man who won tonight hasn't introduced me to anybody.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I don't introduce you because I'm not sure the invite covers you.

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: What?

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: The flyer says open entry. That's the whole reason I came here and it's the reason I keep winning, because if I win it's a fact and not a request. But I've been qualifying *for* two seasons now

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: and every time somebody asks who's on my sheet I say "me and my crew" and there's never been a crew. There's been me. *(Beat.)*And I didn't want to find out what happens to the promise when the

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: person it was for turns up and turns out to be bad at cards.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You're not bad at cards.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I lost to Promoter. Twice this season.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Everybody loses to Promoter.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Everybody's not out there telling Promoter he was representing somebody.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: He's not representing anybody. He never was. That's what's been wrong with this place for four years — everybody's got a crew except the guy who's actually got one, so he turned up alone and then

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: we all decided that was him being smug about it.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Sit down. Both of you. You're on the sheet for the championship round, and the sheet's got two names on it now instead of one, and I write the sheets, so that's a Thursday problem and not a you

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: problem.

postDialogue.speaker: Rae
postDialogue.text: I told you the car would make it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You did.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: You know what, that's the first useful thing anybody's said at one of these in about four years. I want it noted. I'm going to be annoyed about it for the rest of the night.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Cornball—

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: No, I mean it, and then I'm done. The man came out here to win one, and he did, and then he spent his whole night doing somebody else's paperwork instead of enjoying it, and I had a whole bit

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: ready about that and I can't use any of it now.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Quietly, to Cracked Head, who does not have to answer.)* I would've introduced them.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Yeah.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I would've said "this is my guy" and they'd have gotten a seat in a second.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Yeah. *(Beat.)* You said it because they're the one standing here, Blue. I said it too, when I was you. It was never a no. It was a way of saying the no without having to call it that.

starObjectives.description: Use SQUABBLE before the encounter ends.

tips: Continue the story at your own pace.

scenes.speaker: Live Streamer
scenes.text: Final count's in. We covered next month's lights and the room hire. Nobody touches that envelope except Wifey.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: May I stand near it and feel successful?

scenes.speaker: Bottle Girl
scenes.text: No.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: May I stand near it and feel *adjacent* to success?

scenes.speaker: Bottle Girl
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Two feet.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: *(Carrying three chairs he was not asked to carry.)* Where do these go?

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Against that wall. *(Beat.)* Thanks for asking instead of announcing that you're helping.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: Yeah. Well.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Promoter. This is not the list we signed.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: *(Taking it. Looking at it for about four seconds.)* Cracked Head's name is crossed out.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Who took the original off the bar?

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I did.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Don't. Whatever it is, whatever you're about to say — I know what I did and I know what it looks like and I would rather say the whole thing than have six people say it for me in six different

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: orders.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: You *waited* until he'd finished the chairs.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Blue.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I know what you'll say. You were on his *side* for four years and he *is* your brother, and I know. And I want you to say it, and I want you to say it where he can hear it, and I want him to hear

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: me say that I *know* that you were.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Very quietly.)* Say the rest.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: I watched everybody line up for pictures with him. Again. Like he never left. *(Beat.)*And I got a pen and I got angry. That's the whole thing. There's no *reason*. There is no *binder*. I didn't

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: do it because of a *tape* or a *list* or a *four-year-old grudge*. I did it because he was carrying a *plate* to a *table* and there were *six people taking photographs of him carrying it*, and I

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: thought: *nobody is going to ask me to carry anything today.*

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I asked you to carry the plate.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *(Quietly.)* That's the one you've been carrying since March.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* What?

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I don't mean the *pen*. I mean *"nobody is going to ask me to carry anything today."* *(Beat.)*That's not about tonight, son. That was true *before* he went, and you were *nine*, and you *learned*

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: it, and it's the reason I bought you a deck and not a *guitar*, and I have never once said that to you and I am saying it now because I have got about eleven weeks and *this is the last thing I am

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: going to be useful for.*

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Bring both copies tomorrow. You're explaining it before we start. *(Beat.)*And I'm not hiding this for you. And I'm not *punishing* you either, because I don't think you did it to win anything.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*I think you did it to be *asked for*, and there's not a rule on this island about that, and *that's the part that's a problem*, and if somebody in a nice jacket comes next month and gives

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: out a *jacket*, every person on this block will take it and call it a *prize*.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: I've got the footage. Full minute. I can put it up tonight, or I can hold it.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Your choice, honestly.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* *(And the whole arc, in one decision, and it costs him the clip.)* *(He puts the phone in his pocket.)* Ask him. In front of everybody. And I don't post it either way.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Why?

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: Because it's *not mine*, that's why. And I want somebody to *see* me not having it, because I've been a person who *has* it for eight years and I would like to know what the *room* does when I

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: don't.
